Background & Profile

About Me

My Passion for Computer Engineering

As a first-year Computer Engineering student at Mapúa University, I am thrilled to dive into the intersection of physical electronics and software logic. My journey began with curiosity about how basic transistors compile into powerful processors that drive modern computing.

I am currently building my core competence in procedural programming, discrete mathematics, and fundamental logic circuit analysis. My goal is to master embedded systems and hardware-software integration as I progress through my academic terms.

Trigonometry, Coding, Python, and Game Development.

Reflections & Growth

My Freshman Journey at Mapúa

Transitioning to College Life & The Quad Semester Pace

Stepping into Mapúa University as a first-year Computer Engineering student was both exhilarating and demanding. Coming straight from senior high school, where we followed a two-semester system, adjusting to Mapúa's quad semester system was hard. It is not easy to change from a 2-semester setup to a quad semester, and Mapúa is fast-paced, so it felt like sprinting right out of the starting blocks. Weeks fly by with intense calculus problem sets, rigorous C programming lab tasks, and theoretical logic circuit examinations.

One major hurdle I faced during my first term was managing time effectively between heavy math derivations and debugging pointer errors in my C programs. There were late nights when code refused to compile just hours before a major deadline. However, by establishing a structured daily schedule, forming study groups with fellow freshmen, and utilizing campus consultation hours, I learned how to tackle complex problems methodically.

This freshman journey has shaped my technical discipline and personal resolve. It taught me that engineering is not just about getting the right answer on the first try, but about having the persistence to troubleshoot, learn from errors, and continually improve.

Meeting new friends in Mapúa

Meeting these people built my confidence in Mapúa. Each and every one of them showed me how to believe in myself.
